Subject: Proposal: shift to committed throughput + auto-scale guardrail

Hi Eva —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Per our conversation with the product and infra teams, we put together a short proposal that moves Novaretail from a purely consumption plan to a committed monthly throughput model with an embedded auto-scale guardrail to handle peak spikes. The goals are: predictable unit economics for you, burst capacity for marketing spikes, and a safe fallback if usage exceeds commitments.

High level:
- Monthly committed tokens: 120M tokens (baseline) with a 30% burst pocket for seasonal spikes.
- Rate limits per route: 250 rps per model pool; soft throttle kicks in at sustained 85% of provisioned throughput.
- Auto-scale guardrail: automatic short-term scale (up to 2.5x) with price smoothing and an approval threshold for multi-hour expansions.

I've attached a one-page Commitment_Addendum_v2.pdf and a draft SOW. Can you confirm whether this aligns with Novaretail's procurement expectations so we can route to legal?

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm appetite for committed baseline + burst pocket (reply).
2) We send pricing and SOW for internal review (we'll copy procurement).
3) Once SOW is agreed, we issue a DocuSign package and schedule onboarding for the new rate lanes.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call this week if helpful.

Best,

Eva —

Great questions. High-level answers below; I'll have Ben and Karthik add specifics into the SOW and pricing sheet.

- Burst visibility & billing: real-time dashboard (Console route-level view) + daily summary emails; overage billing is pro-rated hourly and pulled into the next monthly invoice with a rate discount applied to burst consumption (we apply a 15% discount to usage within the burst pocket; anything beyond the burst is billed at standard overage rate). We can include usage alerts to notify Novaretail at 70% and 90% of committed baseline.
- SLA credits: yes, standard SLA credit language is in our agreements for downtime beyond the SLA window. For soft-throttle events we classify them as 'performance mitigation' rather than downtime; however, we can include a separate credit tier if throttling exceeds 5% of monthly request volume and impacts P95 latency targets.

I'll ask Karthik to confirm the operational guardrail wording for the SOW and Ben to attach the pricing. If you agree to a 12-month term, we'll draft the DocuSign envelope once legal signs off.

Best,

Marissa / Ben —

Technical clarifications for the SOW (to paste into section 3.2 'Throughput & Controls'):
- Provisioning model: baseline capacity mapped to a dedicated model pool per Novaretail tenant. Baseline autoscale target: maintain median latency P95 <= 350ms for text-gen routes at baseline.
- Burst pocket: short-lived KD (keep-deadline) bursts allowed up to 30% in a 24h window; sustained bursts >24h will trigger a notification and throttle-safeguard (rate-limiter) that transitions to capacity isolation for affected routes.
- Soft throttle: we will implement graceful shedding at route-level (queue + 429 hints) with exponential backoff headers so client SDKs can respect retry budgets.
- Observability: token-level billing export, route-level time-series, and a daily quota report for procurement.

I'll include the exact rate-limit numbers and headers in the SOW draft. Also flagging: if Novaretail uses cross-region failover, rates/latency guarantees change — need to capture in a clause.
